pos.personaBrief: Dortmund won through Gegenpressing and fast vertical counters (Spielverlagerung 2011; Sky: defending deep suited their counter-attacking), with only a pre-season Ballbesitz focus and Sahin helping against deep opponents; Klopp says he cannot coach Wenger's way.

pro.personaBrief: Hummels organised build-up looking for a vertical line-breaking pass, transitions aimed to enter the final third as soon as possible, and the 2013 final relied on long balls to Lewandowski.

est.personaBrief: Drilled 'organised chaos' from a 4-2-3-1 that became a 2-2-6 in possession, with the attacking three pushing into the middle, wide men tucked in and quick players combining in tight spaces (Spielverlagerung 2011, BTL, Sky).

lar.personaBrief: Narrow attacking shape (TFA), Grosskreutz and Blaszczykowski tucking inside with full-backs pushing high (Sky, BTL), creators like Kagawa, Götze and Reus central; Blaszczykowski still offered some classic width.

blo.personaBrief: Gegenpressing directly after losing the ball (Spielverlagerung 2011), usually from a medium block rather than a full-pitch press (Sky), but with high direct attacking pressing against Madrid and Bayern in 2013.

mar.personaBrief: Raum-Deckung closing passing lanes and a compact 4-5-1 block (BTL), controlling key points and pass routes in the final (Spielverlagerung 2013); Klopp calls ball-oriented zonal defending his base, with man-oriented pressing jumps.

pla.personaBrief: Klopp imposed a Gegenpressing identity he kept against Bayern and Madrid, while adapting details per opponent (isolate Alonso, back three when Gündogan was marked; schwatzgelb on tactical flexibility).

res.personaBrief: Klopp's 'heavy metal, always loud' football aimed to thrill, yet this was a title-hungry side that played to win everywhere, including away at Bayern and Madrid.

sis.personaBrief: Young players who 'lacked in quality' were lifted by 'superb intensity and organization' (BTL); everyone pressed and worked, Klopp as locomotive of a collective system.

jog.personaBrief: An 'exhausting, fast-paced system' (TFT) built on players 'quick on and off the ball' (BTL), though with technical creators like Kagawa, Götze and passers like Sahin and Gündogan.

bas.personaBrief: Germany's youngest ever champions (average 22.3-23), only Weidenfeller over 26, Götze promoted from the academy and cheap young signings forming the core (bundesliga.com, Spielverlagerung 2011, TFT).

lid.personaBrief: Klopp the 'Menschenfänger' who catered to each player type and was the locomotive giving power to the rest (Watzke), a leader through energy and bonding rather than iron-fist control, while still clearly in charge.
